This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Apiary Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council.
From the very heginning of beekeeping in movable frame hives, various types of beehives have been used

in different parts of the country. Such practice beekeeper in efficient management of colonies. first published in 1959 and was revised in 1969 types of beehives, namely, 'A' type and 'B' type,

of using different types of hives created problems to the In order to remove these difficulties, this standard was and 1981. The standard provided provision for only two for beekeeping of native bees, primarily A. cerana indica.

With the beekeeping of A. Melifera becoming popular in the country and on account of different ecosystem bees of larger size are also prevalent within the country, a need was felt for third type of heehives. The present revision of this standard is being carried out to incorporate the requirements for third type of" beehive, designated as 'C' type beehive. The 'C' type heehive is based on the 'Langstroth' type and has been modified to suit the Indian conditions
Figures given in the standard arc for guidance only,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be founded off in accordance with IS 2 : J960. 'Rules for rounding off numerical values trevised)' . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE
This standard prescribes the requirements for Type A, Type B and Type C beehives.

3.5 Division Board
A wooden board slightly larger than the brood frame and placed in the hrood chamber to prevent the bees from going beyond it, thus limiting the capacity of the hrood cham ber.

3.6 Dummy Board
A wooden board equal in outside length and height
dimensions to the brood frame, This is used in parallel

at the end of brood frames, 'generally, in weak and developing colonies.

3.7 Entrance Gate
A wooden block at the hive entrance usually provided with slots of suitable size. The slots may be covered with queen excluder sheet (see 3.10).

A wooden hoard on which the brood chamber rests.

3.9 Frame
A frame of wood, of suitable size, to hold a comb.
NOTE - The frames arc so constructed that a series of them may be placed in a vertical position in the brood chamber or the super chamber so as to leave space (bee space) in between them for bees to move.

3 'fERM.INOL()(;Y
For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply.

3.1 lIce Space
The optimum distance between two surfaces in a beehive essential for the normal movement and functioning of bees (see 3.9).

3.10 Queen Excluder Sheet
A set of openings meant for restricting the movement
of the queen.

3.2 Brood Chamber
A four-sided wooden box of rectangular cross-section without a top or a bottom. in which the brood frames (sc� 3.3) arc placed.

3.11 Queen (;ate
A provision made on the entrance gale hy a queen excluder sheet (see 3.10) for preventing queen from going out and also enemies like wasps, etc, which are bigger than worker bees, fro III entering.

IS 1515 : 1998 3.14 Super Chamber
A four-sided wooden box of rectangular cross-section without a top or a bottom in which the super frames (see 3.15) are placed. It is similar to the brood chamber (see 3.2) but of lesser height for 'A' and 'B' type and of same height in 'C' type and placed above it when in need. b) Brood chamber (with brood frame), c) Super chamber (with super frames), d) Inner cover (crown board), and e) Roof (top).

6.1 Floor Board (With Entrance Gate)
The floor board shall be made of wood 15 mm thick and the dimensions shall be as given in Tables ] to 7. If it is .made by using more than one piece of wood, the pieces shall be joined by tongue and groove joints. The slant diagonal groove 10 rom deep and 15 mm wide shall be made along the entire length of the inner side of each of the two side-strips of the floor board to insert the above wooden plank in it. These side strips shall project 2S rnm and 10 mm, above the inserted wooden plank at the alternate front and rear sides of the plank respectively. The side strips shall be 50 mm high, the back cleats, 23 mm wide and 10 rnm thick shall be fixed on the shallow alternate edges of the rear sides of the floor board. The. side strips and back cleats should be fixed by nails to the bottom plank. Two wooden blocks 23 11101 x 23 mrn thick, between 45 mm to 55 mm in length shall be fitted on both sides of the floor board in front of the hive entrance in order to avoid slipping of the entrance gate (Fig. I A). It is recommended that there may be two holes j mrn in diameter and 10 nun deep on hoth the faces of the side strips of the bottom board, corresponding to the two holes of the centre beneat.h the side walls of brood chamber. Eyelets should be fixed in these holes and small easily removable galvanized iron wire pieces, 2 mm in diameter and 20 mrn long should be provided in these holes. 'This will avoid slipping of the hive parts during rnigration of beecolonies. Alternatively, the non-reversible floor hoard may be used. The hottom of the tloor hoard shall he made of not more than two pieces of wood which shall be joined by tongue groove joints. Two sloping strips shall be fitted on the edges of length sides of the plank. These strips shall he 23 mm wide, 2S mm high at the entrance side and I () nun high at the hack side and 361 mm long for Type 'A', 431 mm long for 'B' type hive and 560 mrn long for type �C~' beehive. At the back side of the plank a strip of 23 mm wide and 10 mm high should be fitted on the edge of the breadth of the plank and in between two ends of the sloping side strips. The length of this hack strips will be according to the type of hi ve accommodating 4, 8 or 10 frames, These three strips shall he fitted to the plank with 3 screws on each strips.

3.15 Super Frame
A frame (see 3.9) which has a depth less than that of the brood frame (see 3.3) for 'A' and 'B' type beehives but the same as brood frame in 'C' type
beehive.

4 'rYPES AND SIZES OF BEEHIVES 4.1 There shall be three types of beehives, namely, Type A, Type B and Type C. In Type A, there shall he provision of any of the three different bee spaces, namely, 7 111111, 8 nun or 9 mm. In Type B, any of the two different bee spaces, namely, 8 mm or l) mm shall he provided. In Type C, 10 mm bee space shall be provided. The A and B Type hives may have 10, Mor 4 frames and C type hive shall have I () frames,

5.1 Wood
For the purpose of hcchivcs, well-seasoned rubber wood or well - seasoned timber (see IS 1141) such as teak. piney, pine, loon gambhari or gumbhar and nuna (see IS 399 and IS 1150) shall he used. It shall he free trom decay, insect-holes, dead knots, shakes and splits. The slope of the grain shall not he more

than one in eight. 5.2 Plastic if used for the making of beehives shall he of food grade. 5.3 Wire, if used for reinforcement shall be galvanized mild steel wire of diameter 0.4 mm and shall he suitably anchored in the side of hars hy nails.

IS ISIS : 1998 6.2 Brood Chamber
The dimensions of the brood chambers shall be as given in Tables 1 to 7. A rabhet, 10 mm wide and 16 nun deep, shall be cut in the front and back walls of the brood chamber. The brood frames (see 6.5) shall rest on these rabbetted walls. There shall be grooves or notches on two opposite outer faces of the side walls for lifting the brood chamber. These shall be made in the centres of the outer faces of the chamber. The four sides of the chain her shall he joined hy special box corner or finger or dovetail or tongue and groove joints It is recommended that there may be two holes of 3 mm diameter and 10 111m deep on the opposite upper faces of the side walls of the brood chamber, corresponding to the similar two holes on the lower faces of the side walls of super chamber. Eyelets should he fixed in these holes and small pieces of removable galvanized iron wire pieces of 2 mm diameter and 20 rnm long should he provided in these holes to avoid slipping of the hive parts during migration of bee-colonies.

made by using not more than three pieces. It shall be fixed to the walls with nails. The roof shall be suitably covered, if made of joint pieces, to protect against rain.� The sheet shall extend 15 mm down below the top edge of the roof board. The roof shall be made flat.

6.5.1 Overall Dimensions
The dimensions of the brood frame shall he as given in Tables I to 7. The top bar shall extend equally on bo 1 sides of the frame.

6.5.2 Form of Frame
The brood frame shall have the top bar, two side bars and bottom bar conforming to the provisions given in 6.5.2.1, 6.5.2.2 and 6.5.2.3 respectively.
6.5.2.1 Top bar

6.3 Super Chamber
The dimensions shall be as given in Tahles 1 to 7. A rabbet, 10 nun wide and 16 nun deep, shall be cut in the front and hack walls of the super chamber. The super frames (see 6.6) shall rest on these rabbettcd walls. There shall he grooves or notches on two opposite outer faces of the side walls for lifting the super chamber. These shall be made in the centres of outer faces of the chamber. The four sides of the chamber shall be joined hy special box corners or fingers, dovetail or longue and groove joints.

The top bar shall be 23 mrn wide, 10 rnm thick and 260 mm (Type A), 330 mm (Type B) 483 nun (Type C) in length. A groove 2 mm wide and 2 n1l11 deep shall be cut lengthwise in the centre underneath the top bar for fixing comb foundation. The ends of the top bar may be tapered, if needed. The ends of the side bar shall he joined to the top bar by tongue and groove joint.

6.5.2.2 Sidt' bar
The side bur may preferably he of shoulder type or with separate bee-spacer. It shall be 10 mm thick. 23 mm wide for ~ A' and ~ B' types and 25 mm for 'C' type at the bottom and 30 111111, 31 mm, ~2 InIlI or 35 mm (that is, for bee space 7 1111ll, 8 111111, 9 mm or I() 111111) wide at the top to provide one of the four bee spaces specified. Two holes for wire reinforcements shall be made al a distance of 50 111111 and 100 mrn from the top of the side bar for ':\' and ~B' types but for 'C' type. --1 holes shall be made at a distance of .50 111111 from the top. Alternatively. keeping the width of the side bar as 23 111111 for" A' and 'B' type and 25 n1111 for 'C' typ~. separate wooden bee space or metalspaccrs (60 mm x I() 111111 X 3.5 111111 or 4 111111 or 4.5 mm or 5 mrn) may ll'~ fixed to the side oars. This would ensure greater accuracy in bee space between two frames and automatically adjust distance between the centres of the t\VO adjacent frames.

6.6 Super Frame 6.6.1 Overall Dimensions
The dimensions of the super frame shall be given in Tables 1 to 7. The top bar shall extend equally on both sides of the frame. The distance between two consecutive nails shall be not more than 50 mm. As shown in Fig. IA, side strips of 10 rom x 10 mm should be fixed to the dummy board to avoid warping of the plank.

6.9 Inner Cover (Crown Board)
The dimensions of the inner cover shall be as given in Tables I to 7. The inner plank shall be 15 mm thick. On one of the sides of the plank, 23 mm wide and 7 rom or 8 mm or 9 mm thick strip, according to the bee space used in the hive should be fixed all along the four sides of the plank. In the centre the inner cover shall have an opening of J00 mm x 30 mm for bee escape (see Fig. 1A). For 'C' type, however, a wooden plank of 15 mm thickness having a-�,j mm thick and 20 mm broad wooden strip on the borders of one side of inner cover shall he used.
6.10 Queen Excluder

The super frame shall have top bart two side bars and bottom bar conforming to the description given in 6.6.2.1, 6.6.2.2 am 6.6.2.3 respectively.

6.6.2.1 Top bar
The top bar shall have the same dimensions as given in 6.5.2.1.

6.6.2.2 Side bar
The side bar rnay preferahly he of shoulder type or with separate bee-spacer. It shall be 10 mm thick, 23 InlTI wide at the bottom and 30 mm, 31 mm or 32 nun (that is, for bee space 7 mm, 8 rom or 9 mm) widc at the top to provide one of the three bee spaces, specified. A hole in the middle of the two side bars shall be made for wire reinforcement. Alternatively, keeping the width of the side har as 23 mm, separate wooden heen space or metal spacers (60 mm x 10 min x 3.5 mrn or 4 mm or 4.5 mm) may he fixed to the side bars. This would ensure greater accuracy in the bee space between two frames and automatically adjust distance between the centres of the two adjacent frames.

The queen excluder shall be made of parallel wire mounts or a perforated plate of rustproof metal, such as, zinc or aluminum of not less than 1.25 mm thickness. The width of the openings or slots in the queen excluder shall be 3.50 mm, 3.75 mm, 4.00 mrn or 4.50 mm, The maxitnum length of the openings or slots shall be 20 mm.

6.11 Queen Gate ~
A piece of queen excluder sheet having adequate width of the openings (see 6.10) shall he fitted on the slots: of entrance gate (see 6.1.1 and Fig. 3). The dimensions of the entrance gate and queen gate shall, therefore, be� same. The length of the entrance gate shall be according to the breadth of the floor board (see Fig. lA).
7 WORKMANSHIP

6.6.2.3 Bottom bar
The bottom bar shall have the same dimensions as given in 6.5.2.3. Groove 2 mrn wide and 2 rnm deep shall be cut lengthwise in the centre in the inner side of the bottom bar and underneath the top bar of the super frame for fixing comb foundation.

7.1 Finish
The different part of the beehives shall have a smooth finish with the edges trimmed square and smooth. Parts of the beehive exposed directly to weather shall be painted with a suitable protccti ve paint. The paint shall be non-toxic and shall not have any odour disagreeable to the bees. The colour of the paint shall be white, blue, yellow, green or grey.

6.7 Division Board (see also Fig. IE)
The dimensions of the division board shall be as given in Tables 1 to 7. A top bar, 23 mrn wide and 16 nun thick, shall be fixed to the board, with nails, so that it extends equally on both sides of the hoard. The distance between two consecutive nails shall be not more than 50 mm. The division board shall have a slope, at its bottom edge, corresponding to the slope of the floor hoard. As shown in Fig. I A side strips of 10 mm x 10 mm should he fixed to the division hoard to avoid warping of the plank.

7.2 Joints
All joints shall be sound and shall withstand normal use. Walls of chambers and roof shall be jointed by special hox corner joints or finger joints or dovetail joints or tongue ana goovc Joints properly nailed (see Fig. 3A and 3B).

6.8 Dummy Board (see also Fig. IE)
The dimensions of the dUI111ny hoard shall be as given in Tables I to 7. A top bar, 23 mm wide and 10 'nun thick, shall be fixed to the board, with nails, so that it extends equally on both sides of the board.

7.2.1 When the use of nails for joints is specified, there shall be one nail at each end. The distance between two 'consecutive nails shall be not ITIOre than

8.1 Packing
The beehive shall be supplied in the complete form, properly assembled or in separate parts as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor. Unless otherwise specified, the beehive parts shall be packed according to trade practices in such a way as to protect them from damage in transit and during storage.

c) Date of manufacture. 8.2.1 BIS Certification Marking
The product may also be marked with the Standard

Mark.
8.2.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

8.2 Marking
The following information shall be engraved on each part: a) Name of the part and its size (for example, Brood chamber, Type A, Bee space 8 mm);

Bureau of Indian Standards
nls is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in .any form

without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free usc, in the course 'of
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.

Review of Indian Standards
Amendments are issued to standards as t.he need arises on the basis of comments, Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along wit.h amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes arc needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards: Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. FAD 3 (491).
